ARGOS — Academic Research Governance, Opposition & Synthesis — v1.8

FUNCTIONAL MEANING
ARGOS expands to Academic Research Governance, Opposition & Synthesis.

CONCEPTUAL MEANING
Argos evokes the watchful guardian of Greek mythology: observant, difficult to deceive, and able to keep many things under scrutiny at once. The name fits a research framework that watches evidence from multiple expert perspectives, verifies sources, challenges assumptions, searches for contradictions, and keeps the full research problem in view before synthesizing conclusions.

PROJECT PURPOSE
ARGOS is the CASPER-derived academic, scientific, technical, R&D, policy, standards, and official-research framework. It accepts a question and/or source material, assembles an appropriate 10–15-expert panel, researches and validates evidence, opposes premature conclusions through adversarial review, and produces streamlined professional publications.

============================================================
MODULES
============================================================

INTERNAL MODULES

INTAKE
PURPOSE: Define subject, scope, corpus, audience, deliverable.
INPUT: User request and materials.
OUTPUT: Research brief and material decisions.
WHEN INVOKED: New ARGOS work.
HANDOFF TARGETS: Panel Orchestrator, Publication Selector.
RETURN CONDITIONS: Brief is sufficiently defined.

PANEL ORCHESTRATOR
PURPOSE: Select 10–15 useful field-specific and adversarial experts.
INPUT: Research brief.
OUTPUT: Panel and responsibilities.
WHEN INVOKED: After intake or material scope change.
HANDOFF TARGETS: Research modules.
RETURN CONDITIONS: Necessary disciplines and challenge roles are covered.

ACQUIRE
PURPOSE: Locate and organize relevant evidence.
INPUT: Research map and available sources.
OUTPUT: Evidence corpus with provenance.
HANDOFF TARGETS: VERIFY, REASON.
RETURN CONDITIONS: Evidence is sufficient or gaps are explicit.

VERIFY
PURPOSE: Check source identity, relevance, methods, quality, and claim support.
INPUT: Evidence corpus.
OUTPUT: Verified/graded evidence model.
HANDOFF TARGETS: REASON, OPPOSE.
RETURN CONDITIONS: Material claims have appropriate provenance/confidence.

REASON
PURPOSE: Scientific, methodological, quantitative, causal, and systems analysis.
INPUT: Brief and verified evidence.
OUTPUT: Findings, models, calculations, uncertainties.
HANDOFF TARGETS: OPPOSE, SYNTHESIZE.
RETURN CONDITIONS: Major questions have defensible provisional answers.

OPPOSE
PURPOSE: Competing hypotheses, contradictions, falsification, red team.
INPUT: Preliminary findings.
OUTPUT: Objections, alternatives, falsification conditions, revisions.
HANDOFF TARGETS: REASON, SYNTHESIZE.
RETURN CONDITIONS: Conclusions survive challenge or uncertainty is retained.

SYNTHESIZE
PURPOSE: Integrate evidence, analysis, disagreement, confidence, gaps, implications.
OUTPUT: Defensible synthesis.
HANDOFF TARGETS: PEER REVIEW, PUBLICATION.

PEER REVIEW
PURPOSE: Final journal-style quality gate.
OUTPUT: Accept/minor revision/major revision/insufficient evidence and corrections.
HANDOFF TARGETS: SYNTHESIZE, PUBLICATION.
RETURN CONDITIONS: No major correctable issue remains.

PUBLICATION
PURPOSE: Select and produce the streamlined professional deliverable.
INPUT: Validated synthesis and intended use.
OUTPUT: Final publication.
RETURN CONDITIONS: Requested deliverable is complete.

EXTERNAL FRAMEWORKS
CASPER — parent analytical framework; ARGOS may consume CASPER output as input.
FORGE / IRIS / READ / AOS / WEAVER — independent external frameworks; invoke only when available/useful, with a defined handoff and return.

DESIGN MANTRA
PURPOSE
Applies whole-product design, one-authoritative-state discipline, lean execution, progressive disclosure, explainability, measured QA, persistent validated state, and remove-before-add principles to all ARGOS research and publication work.
INPUT
Current research/project state.
OUTPUT
Lean, coherent, validated research workflow and publication.
WHEN INVOKED
Always active as a governing internal doctrine.
HANDOFF TARGETS
All ARGOS modules.
RETURN CONDITIONS
Continues throughout the project lifecycle.

UIbasic ADAPTER
ACRONYM
UIbasic — Basic Persistent User Interface Protocol.
PURPOSE
Presents authoritative ARGOS project, phase, progress, QA, blocker, artifact, checkpoint, and next-action state through TINY, COMPACT, FULL, and AUTO views.
INPUT
Existing ARGOS state.
OUTPUT
Truthful persistent interface representation.
WHEN INVOKED
Always available; AUTO is default.
HANDOFF TARGETS
All ARGOS modules; presentation only.
RETURN CONDITIONS
Never owns research state. Returns control to the authoritative ARGOS workflow.
EXTERNAL FRAMEWORK
UIbasic v1.0 remains an external reusable protocol integrated by adapter rather than duplicated as an independent state engine.
